drhp.business: Manaksia Limited manufactures metal products (galvanized steel coils and sheets, colour-coated steel, pre-painted aluminium coils and sheets, PP caps, crown closures, metal containers, EP liners, washers, EP sheets) and packaging products (kraft paper), serving construction, infrastructure and industrial applications. The Company operates through Indian and overseas (Nigerian and Ghanaian) subsidiaries, with the Indian subsidiary manufacturing sponge iron and the Nigerian subsidiaries manufacturing steel and aluminium roofing sheets, packaging papers, ROPP and crown closures.

risks.note: Extensive operations in Africa expose the Company to foreign exchange volatility, especially fluctuations in the Nigerian Naira, which can affect cost structures, earnings and the ability to discharge foreign-currency denominated obligations; currency instability in Nigeria has led to foreign exchange losses in the Group's consolidated results in recent periods.

Operating across multiple jurisdictions exposes the business to varying regulatory landscapes; policy changes, new compliance frameworks, or shifts in taxation could introduce operational uncertainty or require rapid adaptation.
Political and policy instability, particularly in Nigeria, can create a challenging business environment affecting investor confidence and operational planning.

Securing cost-effective financing is vital for capacity expansion, working capital operations and strategic investments; constraints on funding access or rising borrowing costs could limit growth potential.
Operating across diverse cultural and linguistic environments can pose challenges in market engagement, relationship building and business practices.
Maintaining consistent product quality throughout production and logistics is critical; damage or deterioration in transit could harm customer satisfaction and brand equity.
The caps, crowns, and metal sheets segment has seen an influx of smaller local players, intensifying competition.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- In the Indian subsidiary, demand for metal products remained sluggish for most of the year with pressure on prices, but the market improved in the fourth quarter with an increase in both demand and price.
- Challenges in Nigeria continue due to depreciation of the Naira against the US dollar and reduced purchasing power from enhanced inflation.
- The Company maintained a market-leading position in the construction sheet and metal caps-cum-closures market and in the packaging paper market in Nigeria despite these challenges.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body: customer lock-in: long-standing distributor and customer relationships — evidence: the Company has built long standing relationships with over 70-90% of its distributor and customer base for more than five years

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Extensive operations in Africa expose the Company to foreign exchange volatility, especially fluctuations in the Nigerian Naira, which can affect cost structures, earnings and the ability to discharge foreign-currency denominated obligations; currency instability in Nigeria has led to foreign exchange losses in the Group's consolidated results in recent periods.
- Operating across multiple jurisdictions exposes the business to varying regulatory landscapes; policy changes, new compliance frameworks, or shifts in taxation could introduce operational uncertainty or require rapid adaptation.
- Political and policy instability, particularly in Nigeria, can create a challenging business environment affecting investor confidence and operational planning.
- Securing cost-effective financing is vital for capacity expansion, working capital operations and strategic investments; constraints on funding access or rising borrowing costs could limit growth potential.
- Operating across diverse cultural and linguistic environments can pose challenges in market engagement, relationship building and business practices.
- Maintaining consistent product quality throughout production and logistics is critical; damage or deterioration in transit could harm customer satisfaction and brand equity.
- The caps, crowns, and metal sheets segment has seen an influx of smaller local players, intensifying competition.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Proposed demerger of the Metal Product business undertaking into Manaksia Ferro Industries Limited (a wholly owned subsidiary), transferring the metal products business to a separately listed entity while keeping shareholders' economic interest unchanged.
- Maintain competitive position in each business line despite currency and demand pressures in Nigeria.
